title: First Draft: 🐊 ‘Didn’t Even Try’ – How Chuck Schumer and Dem Elites Lost Florida
author: Asawin Suebsaeng
content:
_On this day in 1980, Iraqi President Saddam Hussein declared war on Iran. The
conflict lasted eight years and killed hundreds of thousands. The U.S. backed
Saddam, helping him mount attacks, including the[use of poison
gas](https://foreignpolicy.com/2013/08/26/exclusive-cia-files-prove-america-
helped-saddam-as-he-gassed-iran/)._

Happy Monday! It's **Swin**. It's very hard to overstate the [magnitude of the
blow](https://zeteo.com/p/maga-self-immolated-how-everything) [dealt
by](https://zeteo.com/p/republicans-2026-bloodbath-was-way) [American
voters](https://www.youtube.com/live/m4UaAGFTPVs) and the political opposition
last week to **Donald Trump** and the ratcheted-up, warmongering, economy-
rending fascism of his Republican Party.

Democrats are (deservedly!) still celebrating, as their historic wins keep
[growing](https://www.politico.com/news/2026/11/08/democratic-thrashing-
redraws-the-map-of-state-power-01154607). And no, you're not imagining it:
Trump and the GOP are very much demoralized, frantically hunting for
[scapegoats](https://zeteo.com/p/republicans-groan-trump-and-stephen), and
[freaking out about](https://zeteo.com/p/stephen-miller-trump-running-world)
coming legal consequences and Democratic-led probes into two long years of
depraved lawlessness.

And yet… in spite of all the sweeping midterm victories, there is _one_
Democratic loss that cannot be ignored. It's destined to sting in the minds of
many left-wing operatives and politicians, who will long ask what could have
been.

In today's '**First Draft** ,' we'll dive right into what is perhaps the Dems'
sorest bruise hidden behind their collective euphoria over Election Night.
Plus, Trump initiated a farcical weekend of frantic speculation about whether
he was going to make **UFC CEO Dana White** his new White House press
secretary. Really. On we go.

As Democrats cheered and MAGA [sobbed and turned on
itself](https://zeteo.com/p/maga-self-immolated-how-everything), conservatives
tried to find _some semblance_ of a silver lining in the midterm results. One
word they cling to: Florida. The Sunshine State **" held the line,"**
according to Ron DeSantis, its MAGA-courting governor and President Donald
Trump's [former-rival-and-sometimes-
ally](https://www.rollingstone.com/politics/politics-features/trump-team-
waging-gross-campaign-humiliate-desantis-1234872514/).

DeSantis is only _sort of_ right. The Trump White House watched in horror as
they suffered collapses in deep-red terrain such as Iowa, Ohio, Texas,
[Mississippi](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/11/08/us/elections/mississippi-
black-senator.html), and beyond - but the party did manage to stave off losses
in the closely watched governor's race and U.S. Senate election in Florida.
The "blue tsunami" didn't slam into the state the way it did in others. It
did, however, spritz it, even while Trump-backed Byron Donalds beat David
Jolly in the gubernatorial contest and Ashley Moody secured the Senate slot,
besting the [unabashedly left-wing](https://zeteo.com/p/angie-nixon-florida-
senate-race) Angie Nixon, someone whom plenty of influential mainstream Dems
dismissed as destined to lose.

To quote an [American classic](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=pB-bN-RkJLM):**
"It don't matter if you win by an inch or a mile - winning's winning."**
Still, the problem for those intra-party skeptics, and for the Florida GOP, is
that those races were a lot closer than they [should have
been](https://www.orlandosentinel.com/2026/11/04/florida-republicans-narrowly-
avert-blue-tsunami-but-still-get-splashed-by-voter-anger/), to the point that
Florida's Republican elite were having
[heartburn](https://www.axios.com/2026/11/01/florida-republicans-anxiety-
election) up until the races were called.

They had good reason to worry. Since Election Day last Tuesday, I've talked to
prominent strategists and pollsters from the Democratic and Republican sides,
all of whom worked on or were close to those competitive races in the Sunshine
State.

This is what they told me.
